## Source-support findings and smallest supported repairs

### F1 — Altered categories of information not measured (claims 13–14)

Draft: “The report does not measure age, disability, or digital skills.”

Source: “Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.”

“Disability” denotes a condition/status rather than functional ability; “digital skills” denotes competence rather than digital familiarity or habitual experience. An absence claim about one does not necessarily establish an absence claim about the other. Source-compatible counterexample: a report could record disability status but not functional ability, or assess digital skills without recording prior digital experience. The supplied description would remain true, but the corresponding draft absence claim could be false.

Smallest supported repair: “The report does not measure age, functional ability, or digital familiarity.”

This is a source-support issue in translated factual paraphrase, not a finding about a translated quotation or a stylistic synonym preference.

### F2 — Unestablished absence of pilot findings on reasons (claim 18)

Draft: “The pilot leaves that question unanswered.”

Question carried over from preceding sentence: why someone chose phone booking.

Source: S1 explicitly excludes age, functional ability, and digital familiarity, but does not specify all information collected in the pilot. S3 calls for voluntary explanations during the proposed trial; S4 says phone booking is reason to investigate continued use.

Source-compatible counterexample: the small pilot could include some reasons given by its users while leaving the municipality in need of broader evidence across all seven venues. All supplied material would remain true, but the assertion that the pilot leaves the reasons question unanswered would not necessarily be true.

Smallest supported repair: delete this sentence. The preceding sentence already preserves the supported call to investigate reasons. Alternatively: “We should investigate those reasons before deciding.”

### F3 — Absence of a claim turned into a claim of absence (claim 36)

Draft: “We have not costed the trial and do not claim to have funded it.”

Source: “Föreningen gör inget anspråk på att ha finansierat eller kostnadsberäknat försöket.”

The source says the association makes no claim to have costed the trial; it does not say no costing has been performed.

Source-compatible counterexample: the association may have an internal preliminary costing that it does not put forward as a completed costing of this proposal. The source’s nonclaim remains true, while “We have not costed the trial” is false.

Smallest supported repair: “We do not claim to have costed or funded the trial.”

This retains both supplied qualifications and cost uncertainty without requiring weaker language elsewhere.

The draft preserves the thesis, the authentic administrative objection, the report’s counts and scope with attribution, voluntary participation, all seven venues, six-month duration, the author’s support for digital booking, the board’s cost decision, and the three later decision options. It invents no legal obligation, protest, discrimination case, partisan motive, measured saving, personal anecdote, or direct quotation. Its evaluative criticism is recognizable advocacy licensed by the brief.

Completion status: COMPLETE. All factual and attributed propositions in the complete draft, including shared modifiers, headings, and material implications, have been accounted for. Unresolved source-support findings: F1, F2, and F3. No edits were made to the source or draft.
